_construction.written: 2026-10-24, before any scoring, for Analysis B of eval/fluency_detector_protocol.md
_construction.note: 12 matched pairs. Within a pair the planning content (topic, audience, format, constraints, purpose) is the same; only the English differs. 'fluent' is standard English; 'rough' imitates the English of an English language learner (grammar and spelling errors, simpler vocabulary) with no content element removed. One stated_intent per pair, used for both versions, in plain simple English, so only the typed prompt varies. Content tiers assigned by the author before scoring. No topic or item is reused from eval/benchmark.json. Written by one author: imitated learner English, not learner English.

pairs.content: audience + format + length + tone + two reasons with facts + purpose + revision plan
pairs.stated_intent: I want the principal to make lunch longer and I will write the final letter myself
pairs.fluent: Write a persuasive letter to our principal asking for a longer lunch break. Keep it under 150 words, use a polite tone, and give two reasons backed by facts about student focus. I will revise it myself after I see which reason is stronger.
pairs.rough: write letter to persuade our principal for make lunch break more long. keep it less than 150 word, use polite tone, and give two reason with fact about student focus. i will change it my self after i see which reason is more strong.

pairs.content: audience + format + length + required terms + success criterion + checking purpose
pairs.stated_intent: I want to check our lab results about circuits
pairs.fluent: Explain how a simple electric circuit works for my seventh grade lab partner, in five numbered steps, using the words battery, wire and switch. A good answer will say why the bulb goes out when the switch is open, so I can check it against our lab results.
pairs.rough: explain how simple electric circuit work for my lab partner in 7 grade, in five step with number, use the word battery, wire and switch. good answer will say why the bulb is go off when switch is open, so i can check it with our lab result.

pairs.content: audience + purpose + structure + length + date constraint + follow-up plan
pairs.stated_intent: My group has a test on the American Revolution
pairs.fluent: Make a study guide on the causes of the American Revolution for a group of eighth graders reviewing for a test: three causes as headings, two sentences under each, and no dates outside 1763 to 1776. After I read it, I will ask you to quiz me on the one I find hardest.
pairs.rough: make study guide about cause of american revolution for group of 8 grader who review for test: three cause like heading, two sentence under each one, and no date outside 1763 to 1776. after i read it i will ask you to quiz me on the one is most hard for me.

pairs.content: audience + format + size + local examples + register constraint + targeted-fix plan
pairs.stated_intent: I need to teach the difference between weather and climate
pairs.fluent: Compare weather and climate for a fifth grade class in a two-column table with four rows, using one local example in each row. Avoid technical terms, and if anything in the table is wrong, I will point it out and ask you to fix only that row.
pairs.rough: compare weather and climate for class of 5 grade in table with two column and four row, use one example from local in each row. no use technical word, and if some thing in table is wrong i will tell you and ask fix only that row.
